title: Wholesum Foods Distribution, Inc. — Board of Directors Package Q1 2026

title: Investment Committee Memorandum — Initial Investment Recommendation — Wholesum Foods Distribution, Inc.
summary: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund III IC entry memo recommending acquisition of a majority controlling interest in Wholesum Foods Distribution, Inc. at $710M enterprise value (9.8x LTM Adj. EBITDA of $72.4M). Wholesum is the largest US specialty foodservice distributor focused on Hispanic, Asian, and Mediterranean/Italian product lines, serving ~3,500 restaurant and retail customers from 12 DCs. Atlas Crossing is contributing $155M equity; the Gonzales family is rolling $125M (22%). Key thesis themes include market consolidation via bolt-on M&A, private-label margin expansion, tech modernization (NetSuite/WMS), and organic growth in high-growth ethnic food segments. Target 4-year hold with base case 3.4x MOIC / 35.8% gross IRR at a $1.22B exit EV.

key_quotes.quote: The Investment Team recommends the Investment Committee approve the acquisition of a majority controlling interest in Wholesum Foods Distribution, Inc. ("Wholesum") by Atlas Crossing Partners Fund III, L.P. at an enterprise value of $710 million, representing 9.8x LTM Adjusted EBITDA of $72.4M.

US specialty / ethnic foodservice distribution is growing at 8–10% CAGR vs. mainstream foodservice distribution at 3–4%. Drivers: shifting US demographics (Hispanic/Latino market is now 19% of US population, projected 28% by 2050).

Wholesum is only 8% private label today vs. 18–25% at scaled mainstream foodservice distributors and 15-20% at specialty grocery distributors. Migration to 18% PL over 4–5 years implies +220bps GM expansion.
Wholesum demonstrated resilience through COVID: revenue declined 11% in 2020 (vs. 25%+ for mainstream foodservice distributors) and fully recovered by Q3 2021.

FTI's IT assessment confirms the urgency of ERP modernization. Current system (custom Visual Basic, last major upgrade 2007) cannot support: (a) advanced demand forecasting / inventory optimization; (b) integrated digital ordering; (c) multi-DC SKU rationalization.

growth_drivers: Outsized growth in specialty/ethnic foodservice distribution (8–10% CAGR vs. 3–4% mainstream)
Fragmented market with 8+ identified bolt-on targets in adjacent ethnic categories and underserved geographies
Private-label expansion from 8% to 18% implying +220bps GM expansion
Tech modernization (NetSuite ERP + Manhattan WMS) expected to unlock $9–11M incremental EBITDA
Demographic tailwinds: Hispanic/Latino population projected at 28% of US by 2050; Asian-American population growing rapidly
risks: Family/founder transition risk (Roberto → Carmen Gonzales Diaz as CEO)
ERP modernization execution risk (legacy custom Visual Basic system)
Potential consolidation by Sysco/US Foods specialty arms
Labor cost inflation and fulfillment labor availability
Fuel and freight inflation
Commodity price volatility in protein and produce

title: Wholesum Foods Distribution — Valuation Analysis (Entry IC Materials, June 2022)
summary: Comparables and valuation analysis workbook prepared as part of Atlas Crossing Partners Fund III entry IC materials for Wholesum Foods Distribution (June 2022). The workbook includes a public trading comps set (foodservice broadliners and specialty food distributors), precedent M&A transactions (2018–2022), and an entry valuation sensitivity table. Based on an LTM Adjusted EBITDA of $72.4M (per EY QofE) and a selected entry multiple of 9.8x, the implied entry EV is ~$710M. The selected multiple is positioned between mainstream broadliners (8–10x) and specialty/premium food distribution (11–14x), supported by Wholesum's specialty/ethnic positioning, 12%+ growth profile, and 21.8% gross margin.

growth_drivers: Specialty and ethnic food positioning commanding premium multiple over broadliners
Higher growth profile (12%+ vs. 3–4% for broadliners)
Superior gross margin (21.8% vs. 17–19% for broadliners)
Only scaled multi-segment specialty foodservice distributor in market
risks: Multiple compression risk relative to specialty/premium comps (11–14x) if growth decelerates
Mainstream broadliner comps trade at 8–10x, limiting floor support
